messages.content: I have the three San Diego hotel quotes now. Can you put them on the same four-night basis and tell me which one is actually the practical choice?

Yes. Send the room subtotal, taxes, mandatory fees, cancellation terms, and any luggage information for each. I’ll compare one room for Thursday, May 28 through Monday, June 1 and factor in the theater, waterfront, museums, and trolley trips.

Hotel Republic is $782 before tax, plus $46 in taxes and fees per night altogether. It says free cancellation until 6 p.m. on May 25. They confirmed they will hold luggage Thursday before check-in and Monday after checkout.
That makes Hotel Republic $966 for four nights: $782 plus $184 in taxes and mandatory charges. I have its storage covered on both travel days and cancellation through 6 p.m. May 25.

The Kimpton Alma is $1,004 including taxes. No resort or destination fee is shown. Cancellation is allowed until 4 p.m. May 24. They will take bags Thursday morning, but the reply did not answer the Monday question.

So the Kimpton is $38 more than Hotel Republic, with an earlier cancellation deadline and Monday storage still unresolved. Its main advantage is Saturday night: it is roughly a five-minute walk from Balboa Theatre, while Hotel Republic is closer to a 12- to 15-minute walk.

The third is Courtyard Downtown. The room and tax total says $852, but the fine print has a $35 nightly destination charge plus tax. Assume 8 percent tax on that fee. Cancellation is by 11:59 p.m. May 26. They said luggage storage depends on space when we arrive.

The destination charge adds $140, and its tax adds $11.20, bringing the comparable Courtyard total to $1,003.20. That is about $37 more than Hotel Republic and essentially tied with the Kimpton, despite looking $114 cheaper on the first screen. Its later cancellation deadline is useful, but the conditional luggage answer is the weakest of the three for your Thursday morning arrival.

How do the locations work for the rest of the weekend? We want waterfront time Friday and the museums in Balboa Park on Sunday. We can use the trolley, but I do not want every outing to turn into a transfer.

Hotel Republic is the best-balanced base. You can walk toward the Embarcadero in about 10 minutes, and the nearby trolley stations give you straightforward access around downtown. For Balboa Park, you would still use a bus, rideshare, or a longer walk because the trolley does not enter the park. The Kimpton is closest to the theater and slightly better positioned for the southern edge of the park, but it is farther from the waterfront. The Courtyard is near the Fifth Avenue trolley corridor, yet it does not gain enough transit convenience to offset its fee and uncertain bag storage.
Is there any reason to switch from Hotel Republic now that the real totals are close?

Only if the shortest possible walk after Saturday’s performance is worth $38 and you can confirm Monday bag storage at the Kimpton. Otherwise, Hotel Republic gives you the easiest Thursday arrival, confirmed storage at both ends, the strongest waterfront location, and a perfectly manageable theater walk. The Courtyard no longer offers a price advantage after its mandatory charge.
Then keep Hotel Republic. Give me the booking figure and the remaining checks in one place.

Book one room at Hotel Republic for four nights, Thursday, May 28 through Monday, June 1. On the figures supplied, the comparable hotel total is $966, including $184 in taxes and mandatory charges. It is $37.20 less than the Courtyard and $38 less than the Kimpton, with confirmed luggage storage before Thursday check-in and after Monday checkout. Before paying, confirm that the checkout page still shows the same all-in total, the intended room and bed type, no additional destination fee, the May 25 at 6 p.m. cancellation deadline and time zone, and the hours for retrieving your bags Monday before heading to the airport.
